page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v4 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for workloads requiring high memory capacity without the licensing overhead of large core counts. Powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon 8272CL processor on the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The virtual machine allocates 64.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an elevated ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 322 GB SSD, while no discrete GPU hardware is present. Hypervisor execution is managed directly via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Empirical benchmark data reflects the core-constrained design of this instance. Compute evaluations place multi-core throughput in the lower quartile, recording a Stress-ng multi-core score of 3663.17 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 2771.0. Single-core performance sits in the middle range, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1239.0 and gzip compression achieving 24.05 GB/s. Memory performance exhibits stable throughput, posting an average PassMark memory score of 2104.52 alongside uncached read bandwidth of 23.7 GB/s and write bandwidth of 17.49 GB/s. Redis SET operations measured at 3.24 million operations per second, constrained by overall CPU thread concurrency.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the constrained-vCPU profile of the E8-4ds_v4 optimizes licensing economics for database management systems licensed per core. Workloads gain access to the memory footprint typical of an eight-core instance while paying software licensing on only four vCPUs. The integrated 322 GB SSD provides low-latency scratch space for temporary data, logs, and swap. The primary architectural tradeoff is limited parallel compute capacity. Consequently, the configuration is best aligned with memory-bound workloads, including relational database engines, medium-scale in-memory caches, analytics buffers, and intermediate enterprise application tiers.
